title: File Systems, Paths, and Permissions
instructions: Answer from the lesson. For short-answer and practical items, equivalent technically correct wording/code earns credit.

questions.prompt: On a POSIX directory, what does execute (x) permission allow?
questions.explanation: Directory execute permission means search/traverse permission.

options.text: Adds execute permission for the owner

questions.explanation: `u` refers to owner and `+x` adds execute permission.

questions.prompt: A file is readable, but a parent directory lacks search permission. Why might opening the file fail?
questions.expected_answer: Access requires search permission on relevant directories in the path, not just read permission on the file.

questions.prompt: What is an inode on common Unix-like filesystems?
questions.expected_answer: Exact filesystem implementation varies, but names and file metadata are conceptually distinct.
It masks requested default permissions for newly created objects; it does not retroactively change existing files.
